findings.title: Excess room rent
findings.why: (₹8,000 − ₹5,000) × 4 days = ₹12,000. Correct as per your policy.

findings.title: Proportionate cut on Doctor consultation and visits
findings.why: Room cost ₹8,000/day vs your ₹5,000/day limit, so 38% of this head can be cut. The maths checks out.

findings.title: Proportionate cut on Nursing charges
findings.why: Room cost ₹8,000/day vs your ₹5,000/day limit, so 38% of this head can be cut. The maths checks out.

findings.title: Proportionate cut on Pharmacy - medicines and IV fluids
findings.why: Pharmacy can never be part of proportionate deduction.

findings.title: Proportionate cut on Laboratory investigations
findings.why: Diagnostics can never be part of proportionate deduction.

findings.title: Consumables (non-medical)
findings.why: Commonly excluded non-medical item, and your policy has no consumables benefit.

findings.title: Admission kit and toiletries (non-medical)
findings.why: Commonly excluded non-medical item, and your policy has no consumables benefit.

findings.title: Settlement doesn't add up
findings.why: ₹1,01,500 claimed − ₹41,500 deductions − ₹0 co-pay = ₹60,000, but only ₹58,000 was approved.

explanations_en.0: The deduction of ₹12,000 for excess room rent is correct as per your policy. The hospital room cost ₹8,000 against your ₹5,000 daily limit for 4 days.
explanations_en.1: This deduction of ₹4,500 on doctor visits is correct. Since the room rent was ₹8,000 instead of your ₹5,000 limit, a 38% proportionate cut was applied.
explanations_en.2: The cut of ₹2,250 on nursing charges is correct. Because the room cost ₹8,000 per day against your limit of ₹5,000, 38% was deducted proportionately.
explanations_en.3: The deduction of ₹10,500 on medicines and IV fluids is wrong, as pharmacy items cannot have proportionate deductions. You can claim this money back.
explanations_en.4: Deducting ₹6,750 for lab tests is wrong because diagnostics can never have proportionate deductions. You can claim this money back from the insurer.
explanations_en.5: The cut of ₹4,000 for non-medical consumables is correct. Your policy does not cover these items, so this amount cannot be paid.
explanations_en.6: The deduction of ₹1,500 for the admission kit and toiletries is correct. These are non-medical items and are not covered under your policy.
explanations_en.7: This short payment of ₹2,000 is wrong because the calculation gives ₹60,000, but only ₹58,000 was approved. You can claim this money back.

explanations_hi.0: कमरे के किराए के ₹12,000 की यह कटौती आपकी पॉलिसी के हिसाब से बिल्कुल सही है। आपके ₹5,000 के नियम के मुकाबले कमरा ₹8,000 प्रति दिन का था।
explanations_hi.1: डॉक्टर की फीस पर ₹4,500 की यह कटौती सही है। ₹5,000 की सीमा के बजाय ₹8,000 का कमरा लेने की वजह से नियमानुसार 38% काटा गया है।
explanations_hi.2: नर्सिंग चार्ज में ₹2,250 की कटौती सही है। आपकी ₹5,000 की लिमिट से ज्यादा ₹8,000 का कमरा होने के कारण 38% काटा गया है।
explanations_hi.3: दवाइयों पर ₹10,500 की यह कटौती गलत है क्योंकि फार्मेसी पर ऐसी कटौती नहीं हो सकती। आप यह पैसा वापस क्लेम कर सकते हैं।
explanations_hi.4: लैब जांच पर ₹6,750 की कटौती गलत है क्योंकि जांच के खर्चों पर यह कटौती नहीं होती। आप यह पैसा वापस मांग सकते हैं।
explanations_hi.5: कंज्यूमेबल्स के ₹4,000 की यह कटौती सही है। आपकी पॉलिसी में इन गैर-चिकित्सीय चीजों का कवर शामिल नहीं है।
explanations_hi.6: एडमिशन किट और टॉयलेट्रीज के ₹1,500 का कटना सही है। यह गैर-चिकित्सीय सामान है और आपकी पॉलिसी में कवर नहीं होता।
explanations_hi.7: हिसाब में यह ₹2,000 की कमी गलत है क्योंकि ₹60,000 की जगह सिर्फ ₹58,000 पास किए गए हैं। आप यह पैसा वापस क्लेम कर सकते हैं।

escalation.step: Complaint to the insurer's Grievance Redressal Officer
escalation.text: Insurers must resolve a complaint within 14 days, with reasons referring to the policy terms.
escalation.source_title: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 5 Sep 2024 (as reported)

escalation.step: Escalate on Bima Bharosa (IRDAI's grievance portal) if there's no reply or you disagree
escalation.text: Register the unresolved complaint on bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in.
Usually allowed once the insurer has rejected the complaint or not replied within one month, and within one year of the insurer's reply.
